question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Berlin, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

notes.anthropic: Blue-chip powerhouse (Cologne roots, global spaces) representing Rosemarie Trockel, Cyprien Gaillard, Barbara Kruger and Andreas Gursky; the benchmark of Berlin's commercial scene.
notes.openai: Global powerhouse representing leading postwar and contemporary artists, with exceptional museum and art-fair reach.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1994; Olafur Eliasson, Ai Weiwei, Rirkrit Tiravanija, Thomas Bayrle — one of the galleries that made post-Wall Berlin internationally legible.
notes.openai: A defining Berlin gallery with an internationally influential conceptual programme and major institutional artists.

notes.anthropic: Home of relational-aesthetics era figures such as Philippe Parreno, Pierre Huyghe, Ryan Gander and Ann Veronica Janssens; huge biennale and fair presence.
notes.openai: Internationally pre-eminent for conceptual, time-based and technologically engaged art.

notes.anthropic: Historic German dealer with several Berlin spaces plus Paris and London; Albert Oehlen, Bridget Riley, Rebecca Warren and a strong painting roster.
notes.openai: One of Germany’s most powerful galleries, combining blue-chip postwar figures with influential contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: The city's key kunsthalle-style institution, birthplace of the Berlin Biennale and a launchpad for generations of artists and curators.
notes.openai: A central international institution for experimental contemporary art and home of the Berlin Biennale.

notes.anthropic: Johann König's brutalist church space is a Berlin landmark; Katharina Grosse, Alicja Kwade, Jorinde Voigt and a large-scale sculptural programme.
notes.openai: A highly visible international gallery known for ambitious installations and its landmark St. Agnes venue.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1992; painting-heavy roster tied to Georg Baselitz, Daniel Richter, Jonathan Meese and Tal R.
notes.openai: Longstanding tastemaker associated with major painters and prominent figures in contemporary figurative art.

notes.anthropic: Joint venture of Gisela Capitain and Friedrich Petzel in a landmark GDR modernist glass pavilion; Wade Guyton, Charline von Heyl, Sarah Morris.
notes.openai: Influential transatlantic programme presented in one of Berlin’s most distinctive modernist gallery buildings.

notes.anthropic: Rigorously art-historical programme (Wolfgang Tillmans, Isa Genzken, Lutz Bacher estate); Cologne/Berlin/New York with outsized critical weight.
notes.openai: Exceptionally influential, research-driven gallery closely connected to curatorial and institutional discourse.

notes.anthropic: Judy Lybke's gallery brought the Leipzig School (Neo Rauch, Tim Eitel) west; a defining presence on Auguststraße since the 1990s.
notes.openai: Historically crucial to East Berlin’s art scene and still a major platform for German contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Influential since 1994; a discreet, critically respected programme including Klara Lidén, Manfred Pernice and Sergej Jensen.
notes.openai: A key source of Berlin’s experimental gallery culture, with deep influence on younger international practices.

notes.anthropic: Berlin and Madrid; strong film and photography emphasis with Paul Pfeiffer, Iñigo Manglano-Ovalle and Aslı Çavuşoğlu.
notes.openai: Internationally respected programme spanning film, sculpture, painting and politically engaged practices.

notes.anthropic: Longstanding programme of American and European conceptual and post-minimal artists — Gordon Matta-Clark estate, Alfredo Jaar, Rebecca Horn.
notes.openai: A major post-reunification gallery with strong conceptual, architectural and installation-based practices.

notes.anthropic: Gallery and art bookshop devoted to conceptual practices — Tomas Schmit, Haegue Yang, Nanne Meyer — with deep scholarly credibility.
notes.openai: Distinguished for conceptual and research-based practices, especially artists working across cultural histories.

notes.anthropic: Idiosyncratic, much-imitated programme (Danh Vo, Wu Tsang, Ed Atkins, Anna Uddenberg) that shaped 2010s Berlin taste.
notes.openai: Highly influential, intellectually adventurous programme with strong critical and institutional visibility.

notes.anthropic: Nina Pohl's octagonal 1960s pavilion; ambitious, widely reviewed exhibitions that operate at museum level on a kunstverein budget.
notes.openai: Prestigious nonprofit presenting ambitious contemporary commissions in an architecturally singular setting.

notes.anthropic: Karlsruhe/Berlin/Basel gallery with Miriam Cahn, Stef Heidhues and a consistently strong fair presence.
notes.openai: International gallery with a critically respected programme spanning major established and younger artists.

notes.anthropic: Merger of Chert and Lüdde; research-driven programme rediscovering figures like Gabriele Stötzer alongside Monia Ben Hamouda and Kasia Fudakowski.
notes.openai: Critically prominent gallery known for rigorous exhibitions and sustained development of distinctive artists.

notes.anthropic: Cologne-rooted gallery with a politically engaged, institutional-critique lineage (Andrea Fraser, Cosima von Bonin, Merlin Carpenter).
notes.openai: Longstanding gallery bridging Pictures-generation legacies, institutional critique and emerging practices.

notes.anthropic: Berlin outpost of the legendary Düsseldorf gallery of Minimal, Conceptual and Arte Povera art; Hanne Darboven, Gregor Schneider, Thomas Ruff.
notes.openai: Historically pivotal dealer of Minimal and Conceptual art with an enduring international programme.

notes.anthropic: Kunstverein with a major video-art archive and artothek; consistently rigorous exhibitions and discourse programmes since 1969.
notes.openai: Foundational Berlin kunstverein with influential exhibitions, editions, archives and public discourse.

notes.anthropic: Defining gallery of post-internet and technology-driven art: Timur Si-Qin, Petra Cortright, Bunny Rogers.
notes.openai: Internationally influential platform for artists addressing digital culture, identity and contemporary image-making.

notes.anthropic: Stockholm-born gallery in Berlin since 2000; Ann Edholm, Esther Kläs, Miroslaw Balka and a strong Nordic-international bridge.
notes.openai: Established international gallery with a refined programme of conceptual, photographic and abstract art.

notes.anthropic: Barometer of emerging digital, speculative and post-humanist practices; Yuri Pattison, Jenna Sutela, Nora Turato-adjacent generation.
notes.openai: Closely watched gallery representing conceptually rigorous artists engaging technology, ecology and systems.

notes.anthropic: Since 1996 a champion of conceptual and geometric traditions: Sylvie Fleury, John Armleder, Charlotte Posenenske estate.
notes.openai: Known for precise conceptual and post-Minimal programmes and long relationships with influential artists.

notes.anthropic: Since 1997; feminist and globally minded roster including Teresa Burga estate, Anna Oppermann estate and Fernando Bryce.
notes.openai: Established gallery recognized for sustained support of feminist, postcolonial and socially engaged practices.

notes.anthropic: Free public exhibitions from one of the world's leading collections of time-based and moving-image art.
notes.openai: Berlin venue of the Julia Stoschek Foundation, presenting major time-based and media-art exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Swiss-founded gallery of postwar and contemporary sculpture and painting: Tony Cragg, Fiona Rae, Bettina Pousttchi.
notes.openai: Respected international programme emphasizing sculpture, drawing and materially rigorous abstraction.

notes.anthropic: Sharp cross-generational programme (Sam Pulitzer, Oliver Osborne, Math Bass) with a second Los Angeles space.
notes.openai: International gallery known for critically ambitious exhibitions and strong support of experimental practices.

notes.anthropic: Reliable mid-size gallery with Gregor Hildebrandt, Axel Geis and Thomas Wachholz; active on the international fair circuit.
notes.openai: Established Berlin gallery with a broad international roster and sustained institutional visibility.

notes.anthropic: Cologne-founded gallery with a lean conceptual roster including Michael Krebber-adjacent painters and Andreas Slominski.
notes.openai: Artist-centred gallery with a longstanding reputation for idiosyncratic and critically important programmes.

notes.anthropic: Exhibition space of the DAAD Artists-in-Berlin Programme, the residency that has brought many of the world's leading artists to the city.
notes.openai: Public exhibition platform for the DAAD Artists-in-Berlin programme and its internationally significant residents.

notes.anthropic: Photography- and conceptually-oriented programme (Sven Johne, Adrian Sauer, Viktoria Binschtok) with steady critical attention.
notes.openai: Respected for carefully developed careers and a conceptually focused international programme.

notes.anthropic: Ambitious younger-generation gallery known for Julian Charrière, Andreas Greiner and science-adjacent installation work.
notes.openai: Strong international contemporary programme with notable art-fair activity and ambitious installations.

notes.anthropic: Baroque Palais in old Mitte housing Jannis Kounellis, Joseph Kosuth and Bosco Sodi; also Palma de Mallorca.
notes.openai: International gallery presenting major postwar and contemporary artists in a historic Berlin townhouse.

notes.anthropic: Research-based, often politically engaged programme with artists from South Asia, the Middle East and Europe.
notes.openai: Critically regarded gallery supporting conceptually precise and often socially attentive emerging artists.

notes.anthropic: International studio residency programme since 1975 with public exhibition spaces; a main gateway into Berlin for foreign artists.
notes.openai: Longstanding international residency institution whose public exhibitions introduce artists from around the world.

notes.anthropic: Discursive 'laboratory of form-ideas' led by Bonaventure Soh Bejeng Ndikung; internationally influential in decolonial curating.
notes.openai: Internationally important decolonial art space combining exhibitions, research, performance and publishing.

notes.anthropic: Juerg Judin's gallery pairs contemporary painting with scholarly historical shows (Tom of Finland, Peter Saul, Norbert Bisky).
notes.openai: Prominent gallery particularly known for figurative painting and carefully staged solo exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Small, critically watched gallery whose experimental programme punches far above its size on the international scene.
notes.openai: Fast-rising gallery with a tightly edited programme and substantial international fair and critical attention.

notes.anthropic: Large-format gallery in a modernist office building showing emerging international artists in ambitious solo presentations.
notes.openai: International programme recognized for ambitious presentations and distinctive architectural engagement.

galleries.name: nGbK – neue Gesellschaft für bildende Kunst

notes.anthropic: Member-run, collectively curated art association since 1969; a model of political and participatory exhibition-making.
notes.openai: Historically important member-run institution devoted to political, collaborative and socially engaged art.

names.anthropic: nGbK – neue Gesellschaft für bildende Kunst
names.openai: nGbK – neue Gesellschaft für bildende Kunst

notes.anthropic: Feminist and socially engaged programme; early supporter of artists such as Christine Sun Kim's peers and Ulrike Rosenbach's legacy.
notes.openai: Prominent programme foregrounding feminist, queer, ecological and politically engaged positions.

notes.anthropic: Hamburg-founded gallery, now Berlin and Vienna, with a long history of supporting German painting and performance-based practices.
notes.openai: Established Berlin–Vienna gallery balancing historically significant work with contemporary positions.

notes.anthropic: Cologne-founded dealer with a refined programme linking postwar rediscoveries to contemporary painting.
notes.openai: Established dealer combining important postwar positions with thoughtfully selected contemporary artists.
Renowned for politically incisive conceptual art and artists receiving substantial institutional attention.

notes.anthropic: Private collection space for time-based media in a former Luftwaffe headquarters; commissions and residencies for film-based artists.
notes.openai: Private contemporary-art platform noted for substantial exhibitions of moving-image and time-based work.

notes.anthropic: Gallery at the intersection of art, science and technology; known for Julius von Bismarck's early exhibitions.
notes.openai: Recognized for artists engaging science, speculative futures, politics and technological systems.

notes.anthropic: Timothy Persons's gallery built around the Helsinki School; the main Berlin address for contemporary Nordic photography.
notes.openai: Influential platform for Nordic and Northern European photography, video and lens-based conceptual art.

notes.anthropic: One of the world's most important photography dealers since 1974: Bauhaus, avant-garde and classic modern photography.
notes.openai: Internationally important photography gallery combining canonical historical material with contemporary work.

notes.anthropic: Wolfgang Tillmans's non-profit foundation space for exhibitions and projects around social and political questions.
notes.openai: Artist-founded nonprofit with a strong political programme, grants and support for cultural organizations.

notes.anthropic: Javier Peres's aggressively international gallery (also Milan, Seoul) that helped launch a wave of young figurative painters.
Founded 1992 and continued after Weiss's death; Maria Eichhorn, Ceal Floyer, Peter Wächtler — a cornerstone of conceptual Berlin.
Beijing-linked gallery whose Berlin space shows young Chinese and international artists working with digital media.
notes.openai: Cross-cultural contemporary gallery connecting Berlin with Chinese and wider international practices.

notes.anthropic: Long-running Mitte gallery with Scandinavian and German artists and a steady photography emphasis.
notes.openai: Longstanding gallery with an international programme spanning photography, painting, sculpture and installation.
Research-led gallery focused on the intersections of art, politics, technology and visual culture.

notes.anthropic: Well-regarded younger gallery with a strong focus on drawing, textile and female-led practices.
notes.openai: Critically respected programme supporting distinctive younger artists and carefully developed solo presentations.

notes.anthropic: Recent addition to the Berlin scene with a research-minded programme of young international artists.
notes.openai: Highly regarded younger gallery with a precise, critically oriented international programme.

notes.anthropic: Former brewery converted into a large privately funded kunsthalle known for spectacular site-specific commissions in the Boiler House.
Weissensee gallery with an experimental, discourse-heavy programme and an active writing and events series.
notes.openai: Independent gallery with a conceptually driven roster and sustained participation in international fairs.

notes.anthropic: Established West Berlin dealer of classic modern and contemporary German art, active for over four decades.
notes.openai: Established gallery connecting modern and postwar art with selected contemporary painters and sculptors.

notes.anthropic: Grew out of the legendary Maschenmode project space; Thomas Zipp, Erwin Kneihsl, André Butzer's early years.

notes.openai: Rigorous gallery specializing in conceptual, Minimal and materially restrained contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Large photography gallery dealing classic and contemporary names, from Helmut Newton to contemporary fashion photography.
notes.openai: Longstanding photography gallery with substantial market visibility and an international exhibition programme.
Ambitious foundation commissioning large-scale projects at the convergence of art, science and technology.

notes.anthropic: Private collection in a WWII bunker, shown to the public in multi-year rotations; a fixture of every Berlin art itinerary.
Cluj gallery whose Berlin space introduced the Romanian painting scene (Adrian Ghenie, Navid Nuur, Belu-Simion Făinaru) to a wider public.

notes.openai: Closely watched contemporary gallery supporting emerging artists with strong institutional trajectories.

notes.anthropic: Since 1971 a champion of Informel, gesture and abstraction — K.O. Götz, Emil Schumacher, Antoni Tàpies.
notes.openai: Veteran Berlin gallery with deep expertise in postwar abstraction and related contemporary practices.

notes.anthropic: Foundation-run photography kunsthalle with major monographic shows and the C/O Berlin Talent Award.
Young gallery with a tightly curated emerging programme that has become a fixture of the city's off-circuit.
notes.openai: Young programme attracting attention for experimental installations and institutionally engaged artists.
Distinctive artist-led gallery with an experimental programme and strong international critical profile.

notes.anthropic: Spacious Charlottenburg gallery showing established international modern and contemporary positions.
notes.openai: Established gallery with an international roster and visible commitment to contemporary painting.
Progressive gallery known for conceptually exacting exhibitions and influential emerging artists.

notes.anthropic: Istanbul-based gallery whose Berlin space is a key node for Turkish and Middle Eastern contemporary art in Germany.

notes.openai: Established nonprofit presenting contemporary exhibitions, commissions and programmes addressing public debate.
Internationally respected programme rooted in conceptual and formally rigorous Central European practices.

notes.anthropic: Charlottenburg gallery showing emerging and mid-career international painters with a growing fair profile.
notes.openai: Established contemporary programme with particular strength in painting and emerging German artists.

notes.anthropic: Villa-based international art space since 1946; mid-career survey shows of Berlin-based artists with a strong sculpture garden.

notes.openai: Longstanding international gallery associated with significant painting, sculpture and cross-cultural programmes.

notes.anthropic: Long-established Mitte gallery showing German figurative painting, photography and video.
notes.openai: Long-running Mitte gallery presenting contemporary painting, sculpture and technology-related work.

notes.anthropic: One of Berlin's oldest galleries (founded 1968), historically tied to critical realism and political figuration.
notes.openai: Historically significant West Berlin gallery with a sustained commitment to critical realist and figurative art.
Strong international gallery emphasizing conceptually and politically engaged contemporary practices.
Expanding gallery focused on abstract, conceptual and technology-conscious work across generations.

notes.anthropic: Continuation of the historic Rudolf Springer gallery; surrealism, photography and contemporary positions.
notes.openai: Respected photography-focused gallery representing established and emerging international artists.

notes.anthropic: Chipperfield-designed space opposite the Museumsinsel; museum-quality shows of Beuys, Twombly and postwar classics.

notes.openai: Closely watched programme pairing emerging artists with visually ambitious and culturally alert exhibitions.
International contemporary gallery with particular strength in emerging and mid-career painting.

notes.anthropic: Warsaw gallery with a Berlin space; a conduit for a widely watched younger Central and Eastern European generation.
District-funded exhibition space with thematic, socially engaged group shows in the historic Bethanien building.
notes.openai: Major municipal art space known for thematic group exhibitions and engagement with Berlin’s diverse communities.
Intimate, highly considered programme devoted to photography, sculpture and conceptual practices.

notes.anthropic: Contemporary photography gallery with a documentary and book-culture orientation, active at Paris Photo and Unseen.
Specialist in avant-garde photography and Russian/Central European modernism, a scholarly presence on Auguststraße.
Veteran Berlin dealer known for pioneering exchanges with Russian and Eastern European contemporary art.

notes.openai: Respected programme with a strong history in German painting, drawing and materially focused art.
Independent gallery admired for unconventional exhibitions and support of experimental emerging artists.
Younger gallery with a sharply contemporary programme and growing international critical recognition.

notes.anthropic: Rome/Berlin gallery presenting emerging Italian and international artists, with an eye for painting.
notes.openai: International gallery recognized for emerging conceptual practices and cross-generational exhibition projects.
Independent gallery known for strong emerging positions in painting, sculpture and installation.

galleries.name: Galerie Wedding – Raum für zeitgenössische Kunst

notes.anthropic: Municipal project space with a consistently sharp, politically curated programme in the town hall of Wedding.
notes.openai: Municipal gallery recognized for experimental commissions and programmes engaging migration and urban politics.

names.anthropic: Galerie Wedding – Raum für zeitgenössische Kunst

galleries.name: ZK/U – Center for Art and Urbanistics

notes.anthropic: Residency and exhibition centre in a former railway depot linking artistic practice with urban research.

names.anthropic: ZK/U – Center for Art and Urbanistics

notes.openai: Innovative gallery experimenting with exhibition, digital distribution and new models of artistic collaboration.
Well-regarded gallery devoted to contemporary photography and lens-based artistic practices.

notes.anthropic: Small artist-driven kunstverein staging concentrated solo projects in the heart of old Mitte.
notes.openai: Artist-oriented kunstverein presenting experimental exhibitions and supporting independent curatorial production.
Active Berlin gallery supporting emerging and mid-career artists across painting, sculpture and photography.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run-spirited gallery known for idiosyncratic solo shows by emerging Berlin-based artists.
District art association with a socially engaged programme and long-running support for Berlin-based artists.
notes.openai: Active local kunstverein presenting contemporary exhibitions with strong social and neighborhood engagement.

notes.anthropic: Vienna-rooted gallery whose atmospheric Berlin space stages unusually theatrical installations and group shows.

notes.openai: Berlin branch of an established German gallery presenting postwar and contemporary art.
Berlin–Leipzig gallery with a solid programme of contemporary painting, sculpture and conceptual work.

notes.anthropic: Focused on Polish conceptual art and its contemporary heirs; long an important East-West bridge in Berlin.

notes.openai: Focused programme emphasizing reductive, conceptual and geometrically oriented contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run space famed for fast-turnaround, one-evening exhibitions and a fiercely independent stance.
Shop-window space visible 24/7 from the street; a long-running, much-copied model for micro-exhibitions.

notes.openai: Berlin outpost connected to the influential Italian gallery, with a programme spanning conceptual art and sound.

notes.anthropic: Curatorial collective producing thematic group shows and collaborations with international project spaces.
Neukölln project space and residency with a queer, community-oriented programme of exhibitions and performance.
Thomas Kilpper's long-running space for art and social issues in a former butcher's shop in Lichtenberg.

notes.openai: Independent gallery with a consistent focus on conceptually grounded abstraction and installation.

notes.anthropic: Sprawling artist-run network of free studios, residencies and exhibition rooms across several Berlin sites.

notes.openai: Programme centered on concrete, reductive and architecturally responsive contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Artist collective and gallery running one of the city's steadiest independent exhibition programmes.

notes.openai: Important feminist and queer cultural space combining exhibitions, research, education and political practice.

notes.anthropic: Summer-season art space inside a public swimming pool; commissions, performances and a cult local following.
Tiny live-art and performance space with an internationally networked experimental programme.
Artist-run space active since 2005, known for interdisciplinary projects, sound art and residencies.
Collection-based exhibition venue that also hosts guest curators and young galleries in its large rooms.

notes.openai: Municipal contemporary-art venue with a critically engaged programme in a landmark East Berlin setting.

notes.anthropic: Collector-run apartment space showing Finnish and international contemporary art to the public free of charge.

notes.openai: Municipal exhibition space providing an important platform for artists and curators connected to Neukölln.

notes.anthropic: Independent art house combining residencies, performance nights and exhibitions for an international emerging community.
